topic.title: Culture: Elderly people teach children traditional skills
topic.focus: Elderly people teach children traditional skills

candidate_instructions: Read all five sections. Answer Questions 1-5. Follow the stated word limits exactly.

sections.heading: Old skills are disappearing
sections.text: In 2016, in many countries, old people know traditional skills. They know how to weave cloth. They know how to make pottery. They know traditional dances. But young people do not want to learn. The skills are disappearing.

sections.heading: A school without walls
sections.text: An old woman named Rosa decides to teach. She teaches children after school. She teaches them to weave cloth on a wooden loom. She teaches them traditional designs. The children love it. They feel connected to their culture.

sections.heading: Building respect
sections.text: As children learn, they respect the old people more. They ask questions. They listen to stories. Rosa tells them about the past. The children understand that their ancestors were smart and creative. Old knowledge becomes precious again.

sections.heading: Sharing skills widely
sections.text: Other elderly people see Rosa's success. They start teaching too. One old man teaches carving. Another teaches traditional cooking. Another teaches music. The children have many choices. 200 children are learning traditional skills now.

sections.heading: Culture lives on
sections.text: Today, traditional skills are not disappearing. Young people value them. They teach their own children. The culture is alive and strong. Rosa says old people have gifts. These gifts should not die with them. They should pass to the next generation.

passage.full_text:
Paragraph 1 — Old skills are disappearing
In 2016, in many countries, old people know traditional skills. They know how to weave cloth. They know how to make pottery. They know traditional dances. But young people do not want to learn. The skills are disappearing.

Paragraph 2 — A school without walls
An old woman named Rosa decides to teach. She teaches children after school. She teaches them to weave cloth on a wooden loom. She teaches them traditional designs. The children love it. They feel connected to their culture.

Paragraph 3 — Building respect
As children learn, they respect the old people more. They ask questions. They listen to stories. Rosa tells them about the past. The children understand that their ancestors were smart and creative. Old knowledge becomes precious again.

Paragraph 4 — Sharing skills widely
Other elderly people see Rosa's success. They start teaching too. One old man teaches carving. Another teaches traditional cooking. Another teaches music. The children have many choices. 200 children are learning traditional skills now.

Paragraph 5 — Culture lives on
Today, traditional skills are not disappearing. Young people value them. They teach their own children. The culture is alive and strong. Rosa says old people have gifts. These gifts should not die with them. They should pass to the next generation.
